payload.feature:
This worktree carries the verifier and shipper as boxed exec gates as delivered by runs decision-0043-docs-decisions-004-29528051 and this-worktree-carries-the-verifi-131f48a9: commits de7248a, c08c8d4, 923ecbd, ff45ebe and 15457c0 on top of main aa9394c, the second run shipped clean. Its pull request, #173, then failed three CI checks that no seat could see from this Linux machine. This slice answers exactly those three on top of the existing commits and ships. Keep every property the five commits established.

1. Required: `test (macos-latest)` and `test (windows-latest)` fail two brokkr-cli unit tests, `tests::run_dispatch_refuses_io_and_json_then_accepts_a_verified_envelope` (crates/brokkr-cli/src/tests.rs:869) and `tests::resume_concludes_an_accepted_but_unconcluded_operator_stop_and_exits_three` (tests.rs:2198), with "hands need bubblewrap: no `bwrap` on PATH, and the boundary is never simulated; the seats ["ship", "verify"] declare hands and cannot run on this machine". Those tests prove dispatch and resume mechanics, not the box; drive them with a fixture bundle whose gates are fake-driver seats without hands (the shape the machine-proof suite already uses), or, only where the test genuinely needs the shipped bundle, gate it on `cfg(target_os = "linux")` with the reason in its comment. Then read every test in the workspace that compiles or runs `bundles/self`, `bundles/verify`, a shipped recipe, or an `init` scaffold, and make each one honest on a machine without bwrap: the compile-only tests stay everywhere (compilation does not box), the run-and-resume tests either use a hands-free fixture or are Linux-only. `cargo test --workspace` must be green on macOS and Windows without bubblewrap; you cannot run those here, so reason from the refusal's own site (where compile or run refuses a hands-bearing bundle without bwrap) and grep for every caller.

2. Non-required but measured: `bootstrap budgets (60s install / 5min first run)` fails because .github/workflows/ci.yml's bootstrap job never installs bubblewrap while the `brokkr init` scaffold's verify and ship seats now declare hands, so the bench's init-to-first-run refuses at start. Give that job the same "bubblewrap for the hands tests" step the test and coverage jobs carry (lines 114-131 of ci.yml: the 0.11.0 tarball build and the two sysctl lines), so the bench measures what it exists to measure on Linux.

3. The fact underneath, stated where an adopter reads it, not decided here: since decision 0043 the boundary is never simulated, and since this slice the shipped verify and ship gates are boxed exec, so a bundle with those seats runs only on Linux with bubblewrap on PATH — a run refuses at start elsewhere, which is the law's fail-closed behaviour. `brokkr init` says so in its output when it scaffolds boxed gates on a machine without bwrap, `brokkr doctor` already reports bwrap and now says which scaffolded seats need it, and docs/guides/quickstart.md names bubblewrap on Linux as a prerequisite of the shipped gates beside the install step, with one sentence that macOS and Windows adopters need a Linux box for those gates until a ruling says otherwise. Do not invent a fallback seat: an unboxed exec cannot hold a gate under decision 0021, and the model verifier and shipper retired under 0041 ruling 2.

Constraints: the exact coverage gate (scripts/coverage-exact.sh, run with stdin closed: </dev/null) must stay at literal 100%; clippy -D warnings and fmt must stay clean; cargo test --workspace green here and, by construction, on macOS and Windows without bubblewrap; contracts/, fixtures/ and policy/phase-machine.json are read-only and this slice needs no contract change; the decision index docs/decisions/README.md must keep every row main carries in number order; do not name the private neighbours in prose; keep the CLI list "claude, codex or dsh" whenever a list of harnesses appears; commit in the repository's style on top of 15457c0 and never push.

result.notes: Made dispatch and resume mechanics use hands-free fake-driver fixtures, limited the real scaffold first-run proof to Linux, installed bubblewrap in the bootstrap budget job, and documented/reported the Linux bubblewrap requirement with the scaffolded ship and verify seats named. cargo test --workspace, clippy -D warnings, fmt, and exact coverage with closed stdin are green; committed as 9aadfc2.

cargo test --workspace: 57 successful test-suite summaries, 0 failed; cargo run -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self: 1 bundle compiled, 0 failed (offline from the bound Cargo registry cache)

Reviewed 9aadfc2 (one commit over 15457c0) on correctness, simplicity and security. Scope delivered as framed. (1) The two failing CLI unit tests now drive stage_hands_free_fast fixtures: every class:gate seat loses its hands key and takes the {brokkr} fake-driver command, and the keep_review_gate variant retains only the review gate, which carries no hands in recipes/fast (only verify and ship do). Bundle.hands is therefore empty for all three fixture bundles, so refuse_unboxable returns before it reads PATH, on any OS; the refusal site is refuse_unboxable (run, resume, rerun) plus require_bwrap_for at spawn, and compile never refuses. Swept every test in the workspace that touches bundles/self, bundles/verify, recipes/* or the init scaffold: run-and-resume tests against hands-bearing bundles are all under #![cfg(target_os = "linux")] (cli tests/hands.rs, bootstrap_bench.rs, now linux not unix) with the can_create_namespace skip; the #[cfg(unix)] files (delivered_by_brokkr, driver_conformance) drive only synthetic hands-free bundles; everything else is compile-only. The new init_doctor test is portable because init spawns nothing and bwrap_on is a pure is_file probe. (2) The bootstrap job carries the byte-identical bubblewrap step; it runs on ubuntu-latest so no runner.os guard is needed. (3) init warns naming the scaffolded seats, doctor names the hands seats of the bundle it inspects, quickstart states the Linux plus bubblewrap 0.10 prerequisite beside the install step; the 0.10 floor is right because every shipped verify seat and the cargo-detected scaffold bind ~/.cargo as overlay. No fallback seat introduced; no harness list added; contracts/, fixtures/, policy/phase-machine.json and the decision index untouched per the diff stat. Verified here: cargo fmt --check clean; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean; the four touched unit tests and the init_doctor suite pass; the two named unit tests also pass with cargo --config env.PATH pointing at a bwrap-free directory; verify seat ran cargo test --workspace green. NOT VERIFIED by me: scripts/coverage-exact.sh is refused by the seat sandbox (same as prior reviews); the implement seat reports lines, branches and functions at 100 and every new arm (four doctor match arms, the init Err branch, both stage_hands_free_fast flag paths) has a test that reaches it. RESIDUALS, none fixed (read-only seat), none above low: [LOW, correctness, crates/brokkr-cli/src/doctor.rs hands match] with bwrap present doctor reports 'seats ["ship", "verify"] declare hands and can run' from the presence probe alone, but refuse_unboxable also applies overlay_supported to each seat, and every shipped verify seat binds ~/.cargo as overlay, so on a distro bubblewrap 0.9 (Ubuntu 24.04) doctor says can run while brokkr run refuses seat 'verify'; the probed version string is already in hand and overlay_supported_by exists, so doctor could say which seats need 0.10. The init warning has the same gap: silent when a 0.9 bwrap is present. [LOW, simplicity, crates/brokkr-cli/src/lib.rs Cmd::Init] the seat list in the warning is a string literal, while doctor derives its list from the compiled bundle's hands map; init::init already compiles the scaffold but returns only the digest, so nothing ties the literal to the scaffold and a later roster change drifts the message; the test asserts the literal against init output only. [INFO, correctness, crates/brokkr-cli/src/tests.rs:434] the Cmd::Rerun call against recipes/fast stays green on macOS and Windows only because the Rerun arm raises 'has no run/started feature' before it compiles and calls refuse_unboxable; reordering that arm would reintroduce the cross-platform failure. [INFO, correctness, crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine/tests.rs ~3362/3405/3453] three tests compile bundles/self and Engine::start it ungated; safe only because they call decide() and never drive(), so no hands seat is spawned. [INFO, doctor] the seat-specific hands line appears only when doctor is given --bundle; without one the generic line stands, which satisfies the framing once the adopter names the scaffold. [INFO, security, .github/workflows/ci.yml bootstrap job] the copied step fetches an unpinned-by-hash release tarball over HTTPS, installs it with sudo and relaxes the runner's unprivileged-userns restriction; identical to the existing test and coverage steps, runner-scoped, and the framing asked for the copy. No injection path: the doctor and init messages render seat names from bundle data through {:?} and the bwrap_on reason is a static string; no journal, protocol or credential surface is touched. No security finding above info.
